client.name: BizHawk Client
client._kind_source: ⭐ The world does NOT register a client of its own -- it subclasses Archipelago's generic BizHawk client (worlds._bizhawk / BizHawkClient), which Archipelago drives through its own "BizHawk Client" component. So there is nothing for London to write: it installs the apworld, starts that component with --connect, and hands BizHawk the generic connector. Verified 27 Aug 2026 by running the component: it created logs/BizHawkClient_*.txt and attempted the connection. ⚠ This is the shape that has been miscounted twice -- the old survey called it "NO CLIENT", and a later probe called it "needs a RAM map". Both made the cheapest games look like the most expensive.
client._world_lua_source: Archipelago's own generic connector, which ships in its data/lua/. London installs it for the emulator so the player never loads a script by hand.

patch._source: audit_patch_model.py read the world: class YuGiOhDDMProcedurePatch(APProcedurePatch, APTokenMixin)

_note: BLOCKED on the item-delivery path, not on detection. Reading checks is plain arithmetic (duelist win counters, tournament division bytes, dice collection) and could be written today. But the world's client also WRITES: it unlocks duelists by OR-ing bitflags into DUELIST_UNLOCK_OFFSET as duelist items arrive. Without that write a seed reports checks and can never progress -- a plugin that looks like it works and cannot be finished. The write path needs measuring in a running game before it ships. Source: JustinMarshall98/Archipelago yugiohddm v0.3.4, client.py game_watcher.

_build_blocked: JUDGED 2026-08-25 against yugiohddm.apworld v0.3.4 (JustinMarshall98), client.py structure re-read: NOT buildable read-only. Duelist unlocks -- the game's progression -- are OR'd into save memory by the client (8+ write sites inside game_watcher: gold, shop progress, dice, duelists). A read-only module would report checks for a seed that can never be completed. Blocked until the write path is measured in a running game. items_handling=0b111.
